fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Perimeter Fencing; Sport Court
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway are clearly marked with visible address signage at the entry could improve responder navigation and reduce response time delays. Because the property has only one confirmed vehicular access route, maintaining that driveway free of obstructions along its full length would support effective apparatus movement and turnaround capability. Identifying a suitable staging area within the open green space near the main building may assist personnel and equipment positioning during multi-unit responses. Communicating the limited rear access condition to the local fire department in advance, through a pre-incident planning conversation, could further support operational preparedness for this property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Brushland Interface; Scattered Shrubs; Continuous Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Fuel Mosaic; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing direct vegetation contact with the structure and creating greater separation between shrubs, brush, and the building perimeter could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near improvements. Managing the tree cluster to increase vertical clearance and reduce horizontal fuel connectivity between ground-level vegetation and tree canopies may further support defensible space objectives. The continuous grass cover and scattered shrubs across the property contribute to a connected fuel mosaic that could benefit from periodic mowing or thinning to interrupt fuel continuity across open terrain. Maintaining cleared margins along the length of the driveway would support firefighter access and improve evacuation route reliability, particularly given the extended driveway length. Addressing brush concentrations immediately adjacent to the structure should be prioritized, as reducing direct fuel contact with the building perimeter may reduce structure exposure and support suppression operations during a wildfire event.
